flagship.headline: John Lennon returns his MBE to the Queen
flagship.summary_line_1: John Lennon returned his MBE to Queen Elizabeth II on November 25, 1969, as a protest against the Vietnam war, per the Beatles Bible.
flagship.summary_line_2: His letter also cited Britain's role in the Nigeria-Biafra war and the slide of his single Cold Turkey down the charts, per OnThisDay.com, and the clip below is Cold Turkey.

events.headline: John Lennon returns his MBE to the Queen
events.summary_line_1: John Lennon returned his MBE to Queen Elizabeth II on November 25, 1969, as a protest against the Vietnam war, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: His letter also cited Britain's role in the Nigeria-Biafra war and the slide of his single Cold Turkey down the charts, per OnThisDay.com, and the clip below is Cold Turkey.

events.headline: The Beatles' White Album is released in the US
events.summary_line_1: Apple released the Beatles' double album The Beatles, known as the White Album, in the US on November 25, 1968, three days after its UK release, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It spent nine weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, and the clip below is Back in the U.S.S.R., the album's opening track.

events.headline: Incense and Peppermints tops the Hot 100
events.summary_line_1: Strawberry Alarm Clock's Incense and Peppermints was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated November 25, 1967, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It spent one week on top before the Monkees' Daydream Believer replaced it, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: The Jimi Hendrix Experience play their first UK show at the Bag O'Nails
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience played the Bag O'Nails Club in London on November 25, 1966, their first UK live show, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: The band played from the venue's DJ booth, and the clip below is Hey Joe, recorded a month earlier.

events.headline: Harrods opens for a Beatles Christmas shopping trip
events.summary_line_1: Harrods in London opened especially for the Beatles on the evening of November 25, 1965, so they could shop for Christmas, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The band's next single, Day Tripper, came out in December, and the clip below is that song.

events.headline: The Seekers reach No. 1 in the UK with The Carnival Is Over
events.summary_line_1: The Seekers' The Carnival Is Over reached No. 1 on the UK singles chart on November 25, 1965, their second chart-topper, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: It stayed on top for three weeks, per Official Charts, and the clip below is a live 2013 farewell-tour performance.

events.headline: Mark Lanegan is born
events.summary_line_1: Mark Lanegan, later the lead singer of Screaming Trees, was born in Ellensburg, Washington, on November 25, 1964, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He joined the band as its drummer in 1984 before taking over vocals, and the clip below is their 1992 single Nearly Lost You.

events.headline: The Beatles film at Granada Television in Manchester
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles spent the afternoon of November 25, 1963 at the Granada studios in Manchester, filming for Late Scene Extra with comedian Ken Dodd, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: They performed I Want to Hold Your Hand and This Boy, the footage aired on November 27, and the clip below is the first of those songs.

events.headline: The Beatles play their 114th evening show at the Cavern
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played their 114th evening show at the Cavern Club in Liverpool on November 25, 1962, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their debut single Love Me Do had come out in October, and the clip below is that song.

events.headline: Amy Grant is born
events.summary_line_1: Amy Grant, the Christian singer who later moved into pop, was born in Augusta, Georgia, on November 25, 1960, per Songfacts.
events.summary_line_2: Her single Baby Baby reached No. 1 on the pop chart, and the clip below is that song.
